cases.text:
Memoization helpers for expensive lookups in dev tooling.

Cached results are keyed on positional arguments only, which must be
hashable. Cached values are returned by reference, so callers that mutate
a returned list or dict will corrupt later hits.

audit.reason: It documents positional-only hashable cache keys and warns that returned mutable values are shared by reference across later hits.

Validation resolves real paths before comparing against the root, so a
lexically clean name like link/data.txt still fails when link targets a
directory elsewhere on disk.

cases.text:
Lock order is cache_lock, then log_lock, everywhere in this module.

Taking them in the reverse order from a new helper will deadlock against
store() and flush(), and nothing here detects it. File writes happen after
both locks are released.

primary.reason: It explains lock ordering through the named sibling functions that acquire those locks, a cross-function dependency reference; the ordering requirement itself is useful but the named reference flags the block.

audit.reason: It records the required lock order, the deadlock risk of reversing it, and the point at which file I/O occurs relative to the locks.

Yield newline-stripped lines from successive read(n) calls.

read must return an empty string only at EOF; returning an empty string or None
when no data is ready ends the iteration early. A final line with no newline is
held back and yielded only after EOF.

primary.reason: The docstring specifies the reader callback contract and useful stream edge cases, including how empty reads and a final unterminated line affect iteration.

evidence: Yield newline-stripped lines from successive read(n) calls.
audit.reason: The opening sentence repeats the helper's name and visible loop output; the EOF and incomplete-final-line rules are the useful contract.

cases.text:
Acknowledges messages by delivery tag.

Acknowledging an unknown or already-acknowledged tag returns False rather
than raising, so a retried command that sends a duplicate ack is harmless.

primary.reason: The class docstring explains the benign behavior for unknown and duplicate acknowledgements, a useful idempotency guarantee beyond the basic operation.

audit.reason: This opening sentence only restates the class and method purpose; the false-return behavior for duplicate acknowledgments is the useful contract.

cases.text:
Recycles bytearray buffers of one fixed size.

Buffers are not zeroed on release, so a recycled buffer still holds the previous
contents. Callers must overwrite or slice to the number of bytes they actually read.
Releasing a buffer of the wrong length raises ValueError rather than polluting the pool.

primary.reason: The docstring warns that recycled buffers retain prior bytes, gives the safe read/use constraint, and states the error for returning a wrong-sized buffer.

evidence: Recycles bytearray buffers of one fixed size.
audit.reason: This generic summary only names the pool's visible purpose; the unzeroed contents and wrong-length rejection are the useful constraints.

cases.text:
Convert records in batches, collecting failures instead of aborting.

Returns a tuple of (converted, failed). When convert raises ValueError
for a batch, every record in that batch is placed in failed, even if
only one of them was invalid. Other exception types propagate.

primary.reason: It documents per-batch failure handling, the returned partitions, and which exception types are caught versus propagated.

evidence: Convert records in batches, collecting failures instead of aborting.
audit.reason: The opening sentence merely summarizes the function's name-level operation; the batch-wide ValueError and other-exception behavior are the substantive contract.
